questions.search_text: Define the function \(f_1\) on the positive integers by setting \(f_1(1) = 1\) and if \(n = p_1^{e_1} p_2^{e_2} \cdots p_k^{e_k}\) is the prime factorization of \(n \gt 1,\) then \[ \begin{aligned} &f_1(n) = (p_1 + 1)^{e_1 - 1}(p_2 + 1)^{e_2 - 1} \\ &\quad \cdots (p_k + 1)^{e_k - 1}. \end{aligned} \] For every \(m \ge 2,\) let \(f_m(n) = f_1(f_{m-1}(n)).\) For how many \(N\) in the range \(1 \le N \le 400\) is the sequence \((f_1(N), f_2(N), f_3(N), \ldots)\) unbounded? Note: a sequence of positive numbers is unbounded if for every integer \(B,\) there is a member of the sequence greater than \(B.\)
